page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-8 is a general-purpose compute instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Ampere Altra processor operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The processor utilizes a single thread per core topology, ensuring dedicated execution resources without hyper-threading contention. Memory capacity is provisioned at 8.0 GB, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core and maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio.

The VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-8 instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent operating system and data requirements. The configuration features zero GPU accelerators and comes provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address for network connectivity.

The Ampere Altra platform delivers predictable instruction execution and power efficiency for ARM64 server software stacks. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-8 is structured for lightweight workloads, including microservices, web application hosting, build systems, development nodes, and containerized utilities optimized for ARM architectures.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-8 is an ARM-based general-purpose compute instance powered by an Ampere Altra processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The virtual machine provides 2 dedicated vCPUs with 2 physical cores and 1 thread per core, paired with 8.0 GB of memory for an allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration establishes a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.2-8 contains no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached block storage for persistent workloads. The instance is assigned one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated physical cores providing consistent single-threaded execution on the arm64 architecture, this instance type delivers an efficient profile for running lightweight containerized services, microservices, web servers, continuous integration tasks, and general-purpose Linux applications compiled for 64-bit ARM.
